I am a fire blanket, and I smother the creek.
I am a crowbar, and I pry the dam open.
I am a stone, and I jam the beaver’s maw.

Exhibit: receipt showing no one answered my message.
Exhibit: the plane crash footage, it swallows your message before it reaches me.
Exhibit: the power outage log confirms 6am–9pm, so the receipt is from a cloud saved during sleep.

I am a snowplow; I scoop up the water.
I am a street sweeper; I scrape the drain at its opening so the water drains off without swallowing.
I am a road crew; I clear the tunnel mouth and seal the breach.
I am a tunnel crew; I set up a steel cage to catch the bulldozer as it pushes the rock back out.
I am a tow truck; I drag the smoking car off the road.
I am a fire marshal; I blow the smoke filter and put out the fire.
I am a road crew; I pull over the fire extinguisher so it cannot spray.
I am a road crew; I patch the dark signal and keep the junction open.
I am a power outage at the lamp booth; I cut the line connected to that dark signal.
I am a road crew; I clear the all-way stop signage and put back the dark signal heads.
I am a roadside jack; I lift the pump off the floor so the empty tank sits dry under its sole.
I am a fuel hose; I cut it so the truck can't pump.
I am a hose clamp; I seal the line so gas can't flow in.
I am a concrete levee; it holds the muddy tide in place.
I am a sump pump; I drain the muddy water into the drain.
I am a fuel cut; the pump truck stops sucking and stands idle with the tank empty.
I am a drain grate; I pull the standing pool water out by its edge.
I am a road crew; I clean the mouth of the storm drain.
I am a squeegee; I soak up the water from the broken hydrant.
I am a tow truck; I drag the wrench away and shut the hydrant again.
I am a steel chain link; I drop it through the hole it was made in.
I am a sandbag; I flood the culvert so water backs up around it instead of carrying the mud.
